correctness.rationale: For every integer k≥2 and r,s≥0, the proof applies trace-class duality and a jointly concave weighted nuclear norm to reduce the full Schur operator norm to one parameter. Duplicate universal rows/columns are unitarily compressible. The core J-I spectrum yields 2−2/k; the one-shore singular values give f_k(x), optimized by x=(k−1)^2/(2k−1) only when k≤3; the two-shore signed spectrum yields h_k(x), optimized in the interval only when k≤4. Endpoint derivative signs and exact stationary evaluations establish the complete branches. Polar dual witnesses attain every value. Finite checker independently tests profiles, boundaries, duplications and unconstrained small cases; infinite k is analytically proved.

General factorization methods are foundational, not the computed classification. Residual implicit older coverage is acknowledged.

value.rationale: Universal vertex insertion and deletion of a matching are canonical graph modifications in the Schur idempotent norm problem. This classification exactly quantifies when adding entire unrestricted rows/columns strictly changes the norm: at one- versus two-shore sharp thresholds 4 versus 5, with norm saturation at all higher core sizes and no dependence on the number of added vertices. The result is a complete natural family classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice or mere reparameterization; it supplies explicit attaining weights and a robust norm-invariance mechanism.
